name: Swiss Tectonic Arena Sardona
description: In the Glarus Alps of north-eastern Switzerland, this high mountain landscape has seven peaks above 3,000 metres. Its cliffs show, in plain view, a thrust fault where older rock was shoved over younger layers by more than 100 kilometres. Geologists have studied it since the 18th century. At the Tschingelhörner cliff, the boundary shows as a pale horizontal line, pierced by the natural hole of the Martinsloch.
